gaps: Fresh private evaluation outputs now separate db.env, rabbitmq.env and application runtime.env, adding no cloud/API permission or secret. Offline generated-file tests do not establish actual container environments. Database bootstrap and application connections still share the existing credential; separate migration/runtime roles, live fresh-stack delivery and existing-volume credential rotation remain unqualified. See docs/service-secret-separation.md.

Optional operator setup has only offline proof: actual IMDS, Docker/image/Compose/module/security-store checks and ciphertext readback must be qualified on the selected host. Authoritative deployment-binding artifact generation, trusted reachable HTTPS and actual Azure/browser/password/MFA acceptance remain required before azd hook wiring. The host program requires the fresh per-service env-file contract and never repairs legacy shared-secret containers automatically. No automatic hook is supplied.

The optional sealed operator setup transport adds local cryptography and private-output primitives, not new Azure permissions. Exact selected-deployment Run Command binding, terminal-result handling, encrypted recovery readback, trusted HTTPS and real-browser delivery remain unimplemented or unqualified; the portable module is not completed azd setup.

The local operator_access bootstrap/recovery command uses existing privileged host/container and local application-database authority; it grants no Azure/Graph role and preserves other users, service identities and Santa device credentials. Eleven private isolated-database request cases passed; real-browser/TLS, customer private-link delivery, audit indexing and backup/restore remain unqualified. See docs/operator-recovery.md for exact bindings and limits. Metadata is not recovery authorization.

The private real-server qualification tooling uses existing privileged Azure Run Command rights, not a new workload role. Generated Compose and source acquisition need no tenant permission. Community-only production packaging, trusted ingress, operator MFA, unique device enrollment, rotation/revocation, backup/restore and Container Apps parity remain unqualified; private evaluation must not be promoted by inference.

Evidence sha256 fields bind current repository file bytes, not historical documentationUrl content. Existing immutable documentationUrl values preserve the earlier source provenance and may refer to different bytes. The 2026-11-06 reconciliation found only the added PowerShell 7.6 requirement header in the three previously stale Graph scripts; their requested delegated scope sets are unchanged. Current hashes and explicit scope declarations do not prove effective tenant grants or permission sufficiency.

Live sub-mvp inventory found an environment-added system-assigned VM identity and AzurePolicyforLinux extension absent from this template. Existing subscription policy appears responsible; a direct principal role lookup returned no entries, but full effective authority and policy ownership are not audited here. Preserve these environment-managed resources rather than removing them as drift.

The optional VM lab inventories deployment and privileged Run Command operations but does not establish a least-privilege custom role. VM restart, deallocate/start and lab-group deletion need their corresponding ARM actions; no grants are created. No real sync server, device credential, operator API, telemetry backend or backup service is deployed.

The optional local SQLite durability spike adds no cloud/API permission and is not a runtime storage selection. Production persistent state, restore anchors, revocation/deletion ledgers and their exact identities/data roles remain unqualified; synthetic fixture labels grant no publication authority.
Local artifact inspection adds no Graph, Azure, connector or recipient permission; catalog display metadata and this manifest do not authorize grants.
Minimum read sufficiency, tenant consent, Intune licensing and effective current target authority are not proven by requested scope metadata or local artifacts.
Defender Live Response, Intune health-script publication/status, optional compute/sync hosting and cleanup permissions still need a complete source-specific review; existing behavior is unchanged.
Candidate deployment-receipt replacement, authenticated observer provenance and optional notification transports are deferred; no permissions for those future paths are claimed.

Offline candidate drafting adds no Graph, Azure, provider, GitHub or Azure DevOps permissions and cannot publish rules. Sync-provider administration, profile distribution, publisher authority and selected-target live proof require separate source-specific review; enrollment profiles and credentials stay outside Git.

Proposed optional self-hosted Azure sync (#37): hosting deployment identity, resource scopes/SKUs, durable state data roles and cleanup rights remain unselected; no Azure permission or grant is added by the loopback-only model.

Proposed optional sync administration (#37): separate Entra operator audience, app roles and approval/publisher separation need exact-target review. Device enrollment is not operator authentication; certificate issuance, trusted-ingress binding, rotation/revocation and secure MDM delivery permissions remain gaps.

Proposed rule publication and telemetry retention (#37) need approved immutable snapshot scope, rollback, privacy and backup/deletion authority. Fixture approval labels, synthetic bearers, candidate drafts and this manifest authorize no live access or rule/profile publication.
